item.title: Don Lemon Accuses Justice Dept. of Vindictive Prosecution in Church Protest Case
item.description: Lawyers for the former CNN anchor asked a judge to throw out the case, saying prosecutors had “acted on the president’s animus by filing unprecedented charges against a journalist for doing his job.”
item.dc:creator: Alan Feuer
item.media:credit: Tom Baker/Associated Press
item.media:description: Don Lemon, center, outside court in St. Paul, Minn., in February. “The record could not be more clear that Mr. Lemon has been a persistent target of President Trump’s ire before the events in Minnesota,” his lawyers wrote.

item.title: Iranians Say Trump’s Promises Have Fallen by the Wayside as Iran War Drags On
item.description: As President Trump struggles to extricate the United States from the war in Iran, his promises to protesters in the country have fallen by the wayside.
item.dc:creator: Erica L. Green, Zolan Kanno-Youngs, Sanam Mahoozi and Yeganeh Torbati
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:credit: Getty Images
item.media:description: Anti-government protesters in Tehran in January. Iran has executed at least 26 people in connection with the protests since President Trump made his promise.

item.title: Appeals Court Upholds Block on Trump Ballroom Construction
item.description: A federal appeals court panel backed a lower court’s ruling, and made it likely that the Supreme Court will decide the case. But the decision does not mean construction will halt immediately.
item.dc:creator: Zach Montague and Mattathias Schwartz
item.category: White House East Wing and Ballroom (Washington, DC)
item.media:credit: Allison Robbert for The New York Times
item.media:description: Construction on the White House ballroom site this week.

item.title: Prosecutor Sues Justice Dept. Over Dismissal After Right-Wing Influencer’s Claim
item.description: Will Rosenzweig joins a growing list of former prosecutors and federal agents who have gone to court to contest the purge of law enforcement deemed disloyal.
item.dc:creator: Alan Feuer
item.media:credit: Alex Kent/The New York Times
item.media:description: The Justice Department in September fired Will Rosenzweig, a prosecutor who had earned consistent praise, hours after a right-wing commentator demanded on social media that officials dismiss him.

item.title: An ICE Detention Center Roils a Colorado Town and Jolts a House Race
item.description: Tiny Hudson, Colo., was mostly known as a speed trap between plains and suburbs. Then ICE announced it was coming, setting off months of protests.
item.dc:creator: Jack Healy
item.media:credit: Chet Strange for The New York Times

item.title: Bill Cassidy Will Back Todd Blanche as Attorney General, Salvaging His Confirmation
item.description: The Louisiana senator said that, despite reservations, he would back President Trump’s pick for attorney general, giving Republicans enough votes for a majority.
item.dc:creator: Michael Gold and Carl Hulse
item.media:credit: Alex Kent/The New York Times
item.media:description: Senator Bill Cassidy, Republican of Louisiana, said on Friday that he had come to believe that Todd Blanche would be better positioned to push back against President Trump’s demands than an alternative.

item.title: Abdul El-Sayed Talks About His Victory, Chuck Schumer and His Mom
item.description: In an interview with The New York Times, Dr. El-Sayed recalled some of his conversations with establishment figures who once opposed his candidacy.
item.dc:creator: Tim Balk
item.media:credit: Nick Hagen for The New York Times

item.title: The Gadget That Fixed My Screen-Time Habit
item.description: It’s tough breaking a phone addiction. The Brick physically locks you out of distracting apps, making it harder to mindlessly scroll.
item.dc:creator: Rosie Guerin, Caira Blackwell and Christine Cyr Clisset

item.title: Twin Falls Embraces Man Who Confronted Idaho In-N-Out Shooting
item.description: While the motive in the strip mall shooting rampage in Twin Falls, Idaho, remains elusive, a community embraces a bystander who stepped in.
item.dc:creator: Nicholas Bogel-Burroughs and Alex Hecht
item.media:credit: Alex Hecht for The New York Times

item.title: Piece of Plane Flown by World War II Flying Ace Finally Comes Home
item.description: A search crew found the wreckage of Richard Bong’s missing plane on a Papua New Guinea hillside two years ago. Part of a wing will be on display at a museum honoring him in Wisconsin.
item.dc:creator: Ishani Desai
item.category: Richard I. Bong Veterans Historical Center

item.title: How the Reflecting Pool Came to Mirror Trump’s Washington
item.description: A hospitality manager for the Trump Organization traveled to Las Vegas to find a solution to problems at a national landmark. This is the untold back story of the fallout.
item.dc:creator: Maxine Joselow, David A. Fahrenthold, Tyler Pager and Clarence Williams
item.media:credit: Salwan Georges for The New York Times
item.media:description: Workers crossing the drained Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool on July 15.

item.title: Candidate Field Set After Republicans Redrew Tennessee District Lines
item.description: Tennessee’s primary elections on Thursday came after Republican legislators carved up the state’s only majority-Black district in a bid to win all nine of the state’s House seats.
item.dc:creator: Emily Cochrane
item.media:credit: George Walker Iv/Associated Press
item.media:description: A voter left the booth after casting a ballot at an early voting polling place last month.

item.title: Drought and Aging Pipes Plunge Puerto Rico Into Another Water Crisis
item.description: Starting on Friday, the island’s water authority is scheduled to shut off water for rotating 48-hour periods in parts of San Juan and surrounding areas.
item.dc:creator: David Ovalle and Laura N. Pérez Sánchez
item.category: Puerto Rico Aqueduct and Sewer Authority
item.media:credit: Erika P. Rodriguez for The New York Times
item.media:description: Residents of Loíza, P.R., say their water stopped running in early June.

item.title: Fauci Is Far From the First Person to Plead the Fifth Before Congress
item.description: The constitutional right against self-incrimination has been invoked on several occasions during high-profile — and contentious — hearings.
item.dc:creator: Mack Liederman
item.media:credit: Tom Brenner for The New York Times
item.media:description: Michael T. Flynn, a national security adviser in President Trump’s first term, invoked the Fifth Amendment when questioned by the House committee investigating the Jan. 6, 2021, attack on the Capitol.

item.title: In Upset, Andy Ogles Loses to a Republican Challenger in Tennessee
item.description: Mr. Ogles, a two-term congressman, had held off primary threats before, despite controversy. But on Thursday, Charlie Hatcher, a former state agriculture commissioner, delivered an upset.
item.dc:creator: Emily Cochrane
item.media:credit: George Walker IV/Associated Press; William DeShazer for The New York Times
item.media:description: Charlie Hatcher and Andy Ogles

item.title: Blackburn Wins Republican Nomination for Tennessee Governor
item.description: Senator Marsha Blackburn easily beat two Republican rivals and is now favored to become the state’s first female governor after the November elections.

item.media:description: Senator Marsha Blackburn, Republican of Tennessee

item.title: Judge Dismisses Former Olympian’s Felony Charge in Reflecting Pool Case
item.description: The move ends the criminal case for David Hearn, a former Olympic canoeist, after prosecutors acknowledged that the Trump administration’s claims of vandalism were false.
item.dc:creator: Chris Cameron
item.media:credit: Elizabeth Frantz/Reuters
item.media:description: David Hearn, center, a former Olympic canoeist, was accused of pulling up a piece of the Reflecting Pool’s lining.

item.title: Spokane Arson Suspect Said He’d Started Dozens of Fires, Prosecutors Say
item.description: The man charged with setting one of the three destructive blazes in eastern Washington this month also told detectives he had planned the arson two weeks in advance, an affidavit said.
item.dc:creator: Pooja Salhotra and Anna Griffin
item.media:credit: Loren Elliott for The New York Times
item.media:description: Destruction left in the wake of the Old Trails fire in Spokane on Wednesday.

item.title: One Dead in California Fire Started by Man Who Said He Lit It by Accident
item.description: The authorities said they found a body inside a burned home near Sacramento. A man was charged this week with causing the blaze by operating equipment that produced sparks.
item.dc:creator: Livia Albeck-Ripka and Amy Graff
item.media:credit: Fred Greaves/Reuters
item.media:description: A firefighting aircraft drops fire retardant at the Gann fire near Angels Camp in Calaveras County, Calif., on Tuesday.

item.title: Neil Armstrong’s Childhood Home Is for Sale
item.description: In the hometown of the first man on the moon, Wapakoneta, Ohio, the two-story house on a corner lot is listed for $430,000.
item.dc:creator: Alena Cerro
item.media:credit: Patrick Aftoora-Orsagos/Associated Press
item.media:description: The childhood bedroom of Neil Armstrong in Wapakoneta, Ohio. The current owner has collected Armstrong-related memorabilia.

item.title: Woman Who Killed Husband 2 Decades Ago Admits to Murdering Wife
item.description: A California woman who was sentenced to 11 years in prison in 2004 pleaded guilty this week in another stabbing death.
item.dc:creator: Ishani Desai
item.media:credit: San Diego Sheriff's Office
item.media:description: Yolanda Olejniczak Marodi pleaded guilty in the death of her wife, Rebecca Marodi.

item.title: Trump Signs Executive Orders Targeting Birthright Citizenship and ‘Birth Tourism’
item.description: The orders come after the Supreme Court ruled June 30 that President Trump’s previous efforts to end birthright citizenship were unconstitutional.
item.dc:creator: Maggie Haberman and Ann E. Marimow
item.media:credit: Haiyun Jiang/The New York Times
item.media:description: President Trump with the advisers Will Scharf and Stephen Miller, at left, and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, right. The president spoke to the news media after he signed an executive order to limit birthright citizenship on Thursday.

item.title: Trump Issues Tariffs on Key Ingredient for Electronics and Solar Panels
item.description: The administration will impose a minimum import price for polysilicon, a key component for semiconductors and solar panels, as well as tariffs for products made with the material.
item.dc:creator: Ana Swanson and Brad Plumer
item.media:credit: Christian Monterrosa for The New York Times
item.media:description: A worker inspected solar panels at a factory in Dalton, Ga., in 2023.

item.title: Some House Republicans Are Backing a Challenger in Cory Mills’s Re-election Bid
item.description: Two Republican lawmakers have endorsed a primary opponent of Representative Cory Mills, who has been accused of assault and is under investigation by the House Ethics Committee.
item.dc:creator: Patricia Mazzei
item.media:credit: Haiyun Jiang/The New York Times
item.media:description: Two House Republicans from Florida took the rare step this week of endorsing a primary opponent of their colleague, Representative Cory Mills. Mr. Mills has been accused of assault and is being investigated by the House Ethics Committee.

item.title: Florida Man Cut Diver’s Air in Miami Lobster Dispute, Authorities Say
item.description: The authorities say that a confrontation over a diving spot off Miami ended with a boater shutting off a surface-breathing apparatus, leading to an attempted murder charge.
item.dc:creator: Johnny Diaz
item.category: Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission
item.media:credit: Getty Images

item.title: Retrial Ordered in Child Killing With Parallels to Lindsay Clancy Case
item.description: Massachusetts justices ruled that the jury should have heard evidence of mental illness in the case of Latarsha Sanders, who was convicted in the same county where Ms. Clancy is on trial for murder.
item.dc:creator: Jenna Russell
item.media:credit: Marc Vasconcellos/USA TODAY, via Reuters
item.media:description: Latarsha Sanders was convicted of murder and sentenced to two life sentences without the possibility of parole in 2022.

item.title: Justice Department Accuses Duke Law School of Racial Discrimination
item.description: The federal government said the school’s admissions policies, which promote diversity, allowed for racial preferences.
item.dc:creator: Alan Blinder

item.title: Union Representing IRS Workers Sues Over Trump’s Deal Granting Sweeping Tax Protections
item.description: The request was the first time that anyone had used the courts in an effort to directly kill the sweeping tax protections offered to the president and his family.
item.dc:creator: Alan Feuer and Andrew Duehren
item.media:credit: Stefani Reynolds for The New York Times
item.media:description: The union representing Internal Revenue Service workers asked a federal judge to stop the Trump administration from granting the president extraordinary tax protections.

item.title: Mitch McConnell Discharged From Rehabilitation Facility
item.description: The Kentucky Republican has been absent from Congress for nearly two months after a health episode. He said he would continue recovering from home.
item.dc:creator: Olivia Diaz
item.media:credit: Haiyun Jiang/The New York Times
item.media:description: Senator Mitch McConnell of Kentucky on Capitol Hill earlier this year. Mr. McConnell was hospitalized in June after falling unconscious in his home.

item.title: Annelise Camp, Whose Family Sued to Stop Brain Death Test After Drowning, Has Died
item.description: The case of 2-year-old Annelise Camp, who was found unconscious in May, drew the backing of anti-abortion activists. On Monday, the family decided to remove life support.
item.dc:creator: Pooja Salhotra
item.media:credit: Aaron M. Sprecher, via Associated Press
item.media:description: The family of Annelise Camp sued Texas Children’s Hospital in Houston this year to stop it from conducting a brain death test.

item.title: Hemp Fight Snarls Speedy Passage of Government Funding Bill
item.description: A White House effort to delay a ban on intoxicating hemp was holding up a final agreement on a bipartisan spending bill ahead of a monthlong Senate recess.
item.dc:creator: Catie Edmondson and Olivia Diaz
item.media:credit: Allison Robbert for The New York Times
item.media:description: Senator Ted Budd, Republican of North Carolina, at the Capitol on Wednesday.
